artworks.title: Jenna Gribbon: Entwined
artworks.description: The Rose Art Museum is proud to present Jenna Gribbon: Entwined , the first major solo museum exhibition of paintings by Jenna Gribbon (b. 1978, Knoxville, TN). Bringing together more than forty works created between 2001 and the present, the exhibition traces the evolution of Gribbon’s distinctive approach to figurative painting, from early experimental works to ambitious new canvases made specially for this survey. Best known for her intimate portrayals of family, friends, and especially her wife, musician Mackenzie Scott (TORRES), Gribbon creates paintings that blur the boundaries between artist and subject, viewer and participant, observation and performance. Through luminous color, inventive compositions, and emotionally charged imagery, her work transforms everyday moments into complex reflections on love, desire, memory, and perception.
artworks.imageCredit: Jenna Gribbon, Examinationscape, 2021 (detail). Tia Collection. © Jenna Gribbon. Press image of the Rose Art Museum (via BroadwayWorld)

artworks.title: ChromaForm
artworks.description: ChromaForm explores a pivotal moment in mid-twentieth-century abstraction, when artists began moving away from the emotional intensity of Abstract Expressionism toward a new focus on perception, geometry, and color. Drawn from the Rose Art Museum’s permanent collection, the exhibition features works by Josef Albers, Ralph Coburn, Gene Davis, Ronald Wendell Davis, Al Held, Will Insley, Ellsworth Kelly, Sol LeWitt, Mary Lewis, and Leon Polk Smith. These artists use crisp lines, shaped canvases, and vibrant chromatic relationships to invite viewers to reconsider how art can create meaning through visual experience itself. ChromaForm is co-curated by Chad Sirois and Dr. Gannit Ankori, Henry and Lois Foster Director and Chief Curator, and Professor of Fine Arts and Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies.
artworks.imageCredit: Leon Polk Smith, George Washington Bridge #2, 1979. Rose Art Museum, gift of Mr. Gerald Lennard, 2000.83. Rose Art Museum, Brandeis University (brandeis.edu/rose)

artworks.title: Yinka Shonibare: Sanctuary
artworks.description: Yinka Shonibare: Sanctuary presents the U.S. debut of Sanctuary City (2024), a major installation by British-Nigerian artist Yinka Shonibare (b. 1962, London, UK). The installation comprises 18 scaled-down replicas of historical and contemporary buildings that have served as sites of refuge for persecuted and vulnerable individuals across centuries. Displayed in a darkened gallery, each black-painted structure glows from within, its interior illuminated and lined with Shonibare’s signature Dutch wax textiles, transforming the space into a constellation of sanctuary havens that appear as beacons of light and hope. Drawing on his interdisciplinary practice and longstanding engagement with colonial histories, migration, and cultural hybridity, Shonibare frames shelter as both a universal human need and a deeply political condition.
artworks.imageCredit: Yinka Shonibare, Sanctuary City, 2024, installation view at Serpentine South. Photo © Jo Underhill. Rose Art Museum, Brandeis University (brandeis.edu/rose)

artworks.title: En/Lighten: Material & Metaphor
artworks.description: Light as a physical thing and as a symbol, from the Rose’s collection and loans: works made with incandescent bulbs, neon, fluorescent tubes, scrolling LED text and video monitors by Dan Basen, Christian Boltanski, Dan Flavin, Felix Gonzalez-Torres, Jenny Holzer, Alfredo Jaar, Joseph Kosuth, Bruce Nauman, Nam June Paik and Mary Weatherford. The show begins outdoors with Chris Burden’s Light of Reason. Co-curated by Gannit Ankori and Chad Sirois.
artworks.imageCredit: Chris Burden, Light of Reason, 2014, where the show begins. Rose Art Museum, Brandeis University (brandeis.edu/rose)

artworks.placeNote: The museum puts this show in the Lower Rose Gallery; where that room is on this plan is our best reading of the museum’s pages.

artworks.title: The Undisciplined Collector
artworks.description: A wood-paneled room furnished with the trappings of a 1961 collector’s den, the year the Rose was founded: books, furniture and objects from the collections of Brandeis University, which visitors can walk into. It is the museum’s introduction to the history of collecting at Brandeis. Rose Art Museum Special Fund, 2015.6.
artworks.medium: Room-sized installation: a wood-paneled den furnished as in 1961
artworks.imageCredit: Mark Dion, The Undisciplined Collector, 2015. Rose Art Museum Special Fund, 2015.6. Rose Art Museum, Brandeis University (brandeis.edu/rose)

artworks.title: Light of Reason
artworks.description: Twenty-four antique cast-iron Victorian street lamps and concrete benches in three branches that fan out from the museum’s entrance, made for the Rose and Brandeis. The three branches come from the three torches, hills and Hebrew letters of the university seal; the title from Louis D. Brandeis: “If we would guide by the light of reason, we must let our minds be bold.” The lamps go on at sunset and off at sunrise. Rose Art Museum Acquisition Fund, gift of Monroe and Edith Geller and Russian Sale Gift, 2014.3.
